title: Prompt surface evolution and parameter aliasing contract for pinned model versions
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: When customers pin a model version we guarantee behavioral invariants for production workloads. Historically these guarantees have focused on output shape and top-level parameter stability, but we now see two classes of regression risk: (1) subtle prompt surface changes (aliases, normalized parameter names, deprecations) that break prompt engineering patterns; and (2) backward-incompatible parameter semantics (e.g. temperature/penalty interpretation changes, new default tokens) that change output distributions without a manifest version bump. This ticket defines an engineering contract for allowed prompt/parameter evolution for pinned versions and a minimal regression playbook to validate compatibility before publishing a pinned version or serving a new model behind a pinned alias.

Scope: the contract applies to all pinned model versions (hosted, dedicated, and private) surfaced through the Redwood API. Exemptions must be explicit (security fixes, severe bug patches) and require a documented compatibility exemption and communication plan.

Goals: (1) reduce unexpected customer regressions from prompt/parameter drift; (2) provide a clear, automated validation pipeline that gates any change that could affect pinned IO or parameter behavior; (3) define an aliasing and deprecation policy so clients can opt into new parameter names without breaking existing integrations.
acceptance_criteria: A textual contract document exists that defines allowed vs disallowed prompt surface changes (whitespace, tokenization normalization, deterministic alias map) and is published to Confluence
An automated regression job (regression-harness/pinned-compat) executes a suite of canonical prompt/parameter tests and fails on behavioral divergence beyond a configurable threshold
Parameter aliasing table and defaults semantics are recorded and enforced by the API gateway so old parameter names continue to function until a deprecation window expires
All changes to pinned model metadata must create a changelog entry and, for any non-trivial behavioral change, a rollout runbook that includes customer-notification templates
Documented exemption process for emergency patches with required post-hoc audit and customer outreach
decisions: Adopt a semver-esque labeling for pinned model releases: MAJOR for breaking IO/parameter semantic changes, MINOR for additive non-breaking features, PATCH for bug fixes that do not alter IO semantics
Introduce a parameter alias registry (internal only) mapping deprecated names to canonical names; the runtime will honor aliases for a 90-day deprecation window by default
Treat whitespace/tokenization normalization as non-breaking if a golden set of tokenized outputs for the pinned version is maintained and validated
Use KL-divergence on an evaluation corpus + deterministic heuristics (e.g. stop token frequency, completion length distribution) as the failure signal in the regression job
rollout_plan: Draft contract and circulate to PM, Design (ux for param deprecation), and Security for review (1 week)
Implement alias registry and gateway mapping behind a feature flag in staging (2 sprints)
Create and onboard the regression-harness pipeline to CI with baseline runs for currently pinned models (3 days)
Run canary enforcement for new pin publications for 7 days before marking as fully pinned; surface results in the Console rollout page
Publish the contract and notify customers with pinned versions via in-console banner + email for any MAJOR-labeled changes
qa_tasks: Create canonical prompt corpus for top-10 enterprise customers and add synthetic edge-cases
Define numerical thresholds for KL-divergence, token-level change rate, and completion-length variance
Add unit tests for alias mapping and gateway fallback behavior
Simulate a parameter rename (e.g. "temperature" -> "temp") and validate backwards compatibility across SDKs
Run a full regression job against runtime-1.20 pinned models and record baseline metrics in the dashboard
